audit_result.proof_trace: The only guard at L12 is `if (!generation)`, which is a falsy check only — it does not enforce typeof, positivity, integer-ness, or an upper bound. The TypeScript cast `req.body as GenerationCreateRequest` is compile-time only and provides zero runtime validation. Consequently, strings, negative numbers, floats, and objects all pass the check and are inserted into the DB and forwarded to Discord's role-creation API unmodified.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An authenticated caller (holding the API_AUTH_TOKEN) sends POST /api/generation with body `{"generation": -1}` or `{"generation": "malicious"}`. The falsy check passes, Discord creates a role with an invalid name (e.g. "-1期生"), and the generation_roles table is permanently corrupted with a non-positive or non-numeric generation key, breaking downstream role-assignment queries that assume a valid integer.

PROP-stem-bot-v21-pre-004.text: createGeneration must validate generation is a positive integer within expected range.
PROP-stem-bot-v21-pre-004.assertion: pre: createGeneration(gen) => typeof gen == 'number' && gen > 0 && gen < MAX_GEN
